newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell opens community hospital in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Shell opens community hospital in Nigeria.

text.p: The local unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said on Friday it had commissioned a hospital at Okoroba in Nembe area of Nigeria in the southeast.
It said the 35 million naira 20-bed hospital opened on Thursday was the fifth to be completed for communities in Nigeria's Niger delta where Shell produces crude oil.
It will be jointly run by Shell, the Bayelsa state government and the community.
Shell has long been under criticism from pressure groups for neglect of the Nigerian swamps where it produces about half Nigeria's roughly two million barrels per day of crude oil.
The company says it spent 2.8 billion naira last year in community assistance for the areas where it operates.
"This hospital is a tribute to mutual assistance and interdependence between government, the oil industry and the host community," said Shell's manager in the area Chris Haynes.
"Together, we can do more than we can achieve seperately," he added.
